name: attack-rule
question: Our agent kills 0.105 opponents per game against three rule_based agents; they take 0.23 from us. Score is coins plus five times kills, so that deficit costs 0.63 points and is the entire gap between us and the heuristic. Can we close it at play time, by taking the attack the policy keeps declining?
why_this_is_not_a_seventh_attempt_at_the: Six registered experiments tried to teach the network to attack and all six were empty: the elimination reward raised from +5 to +20 twice (+0.010 and +0.005 eliminations), the wasteful-bomb penalty removed for safe attacks over 50,000 episodes (0 points), approach shaping (more exposure, less score), and the training line-up twice (-0.075 and -0.250 on score). Every one of them tried to change what the network learns. The hunting diagnosis shows why that is so hard: a bomb aimed at an opponent with no crate in its blast books -0.5 immediately and with certainty, while the +5 arrives four steps later, discounted by gamma^4 to about two thirds, and only if the opponent fails to walk away. At one kill per hundred attack steps the expected value of attacking is negative whatever the kill is worth. This rule sits outside the network and needs no credit assignment at all.
the_rule: When an opponent stands inside the blast footprint of a bomb placed where we are, and safe_escape_exists says we could still get out of that bomb, place it. It never fires without a bomb in hand, never fires when the policy already chose BOMB, never fires while training, and it uses the framework's own blast geometry, so a crate in the way does not save the opponent but a wall does.

cells.name: control
cells.note: identical play to the shipped Bomb-omb

cells.name: attack
cells.note: the rule alone; the primary contrast

cells.name: attack-guard
cells.note: the rule on top of the survival guard, to decide whether to stack them

design.agent: Bomb-omb-survivalguard, which now carries both add-ons behind separate switches
design.order: control, attack, attack-guard. The primary contrast is finished after two cells.
design.not_under_test: The seek rule, which walks toward a firing position on a cleared board, is built and switched off in every cell here. On a 25-world smoke run it took survival from 0.20 to 0.04 while kills fell, so it is not a candidate tonight. Its switch is named explicitly in every cell so it cannot leak in from a previous shell.

checkpoints.judged: the 12 milestones at episodes 6,000 and 8,000: control-r1..r3 and halved-r1..r3
checkpoints.why: The survival-guard factorial found no decay of the effect across episodes 2,000 to 6,000, and the checkpoint level dominates this kind of contrast, so we buy checkpoints rather than worlds: twelve checkpoints on 150 worlds instead of six on 300.
checkpoints.also_played: the untrained reference, for context only. It does not enter the decision.

suite.name: attack-rule-fresh
suite.seed_audit: All 150 seeds and their plus and minus 1,000,000 offsets checked against every integer of six digits or more in the 947 readable tracked text files on 18 September. No collision, no overlap with the held-out suite, and no overlap with the worlds of the monitoring suite, the loop-guard test, the survival-guard factorial or its confirmation.

decision_rule.type: decision under uncertainty, not a significance test
decision_rule.pairing: the same checkpoint on the same world, rule on versus rule off

interval.method: hierarchical paired bootstrap, resampling the 12 checkpoints and then the 150 worlds

ship_if_all: the kill point estimate is above 0, because a rule that does not produce kills has no reason to exist
the score point estimate is at least 0
the lower bound of the score interval is above -0.15, so a real cost is ruled out
decision_rule.stacking: If the rule ships, attack-guard minus attack decides whether the survival guard goes with it: we stack them only if that contrast's score point estimate is at least 0. The guard's own confirmation is a separate registration on separate worlds.
decision_rule.what_we_will_not_claim: We will not describe this as a significant improvement whatever it shows. With twelve checkpoints from six training seeds the interval is wide by construction. If it ships it ships as the better of two options on the evidence we could afford before Monday.
reported_without_gating: the 95% interval for score, kills, self-kills, coins, survival and invalid actions
how many of the twelve checkpoints improved on score, and on kills

known_limits: Opponents are not seeded, so the same world plays out differently each time; pairing removes the world, not the opponents.
The rule is myopic. It fires on the opponent's current tile and the opponent usually moves during the four-step fuse, so most of its bombs will miss. It only has to pay for itself.

It will place more bombs than the policy would, which risks self-kills. That is why the self-kill and score numbers are reported and why the escape check is part of the rule rather than an afterthought.

We judge on episodes 6,000 and 8,000 of the previous run. If the warm-lineup continuation produces the shipped checkpoint instead, this result carries over as evidence rather than as a direct test of that checkpoint.
expected_cost: 3 cells x 13 checkpoints x 150 worlds = 5,850 games, about four hours with two jobs.
authorization: Julius (1BlauNitrox) asked on 18 September for the agent to stop looping and to focus on escaping and hunting, after watching it play. This registration covers the hunting half; the survival guard covers the escaping half.
